blocks.content: The Mauryan Empire was the first large empire in Indian history. It was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE.
1. Background of the Mauryan Empire

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire, ruling from 322 to 298 BCE.
Bindusara succeeded Chandragupta Maurya and ruled from 298 to 273 BCE.
Ashoka the Great ruled from 273 to 232 BCE and adopted Ashoka's Dhamma after the Kalinga War.
Mauryan Administration and Economy were highly structured and centralized.
Mauryan Art and Architecture marked a significant milestone in ancient Indian history.

blocks.content: • After the decline of the Nanda dynasty, political instability existed in northern India.
• Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the last Nanda ruler Dhana Nanda.
• He established the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE.
• Chanakya (Kautilya) played a crucial role in the rise of the Mauryan Empire.
Important Mauryan Rulers
3. Chandragupta Maurya (322–298 BCE)
• Founder of the Mauryan Empire.
• Defeated the Nanda dynasty.
• Defeated Seleucus Nicator, the Greek ruler.
• Greek ambassador Megasthenes visited his court.
• Author of 'Indica' which described Mauryan administration.
4. Bindusara (298–273 BCE)
• Son of Chandragupta Maurya.
• Expanded the Mauryan Empire towards southern India.
• Known as Amitraghata (Slayer of enemies).
5. Ashoka the Great (273–232 BCE)
• One of the greatest rulers in Indian history.
• Fought the Kalinga War around 261 BCE.
• The war caused heavy destruction and loss of life.
• Ashoka later embraced Buddhism and adopted the policy of Dhamma.
6. Kalinga War
• Fought between Ashoka and the state of Kalinga.
• Took place around 261 BCE.
• Thousands of people were killed.
• After witnessing the destruction, Ashoka adopted Buddhism.
7. Ashoka's Dhamma
• Respect for elders.
• Kindness to animals.
• Religious tolerance.
• Non-violence and moral conduct.

blocks.content: 9. Mauryan Economy
• Agriculture was the main occupation.
• Land revenue was the major source of income.
• Trade and commerce flourished.
• Roads were constructed for better trade.
10. Mauryan Art and Architecture
• Ashokan pillars are famous examples of Mauryan art.

items: Timeline and order of Mauryan Rulers: Chandragupta Maurya (322–298 BCE) -> Bindusara (298–273 BCE) -> Ashoka (273–232 BCE).
Impact of the Kalinga War on Ashoka's shift towards Dhamma and non-violence.

• Stupas were built to preserve Buddhist relics.
